title: The Black Death
examples: What caused the Black Death to spread so quickly?
How did the plague change life for common people?
Were the workers treated better after the Black Death?

explain.say: The plague spread through trade routes and crowded areas.
The disease often traveled on fleas carried by rats.
A major impact was the sudden death of many people everywhere.
Fewer people meant that farming and building slowed down a lot.
Workers suddenly had less competition and more bargaining power.
In everyday life, surviving the plague changed how people valued their time.

faq.q: Why did the plague spread so easily in cities?
faq.a: Cities were very crowded, which allowed diseases to pass between people quickly. People also traveled through many trade routes.

faq.q: Did the plague only affect poor people?
faq.a: No, it affected people across many social classes, though some groups were hit harder due to living conditions. The death toll was very high everywhere.
asks: Was it only bad for the poor?

faq.q: What was the biggest consequence for the workers?
faq.a: The biggest change was that workers suddenly became much more valuable because there were so few of them left. This gave them more say in wages.
asks: What was the effect on labor?

faq.q: Did life immediately get better after the plague?
faq.a: No, it took time for society to recover from such a massive loss of life. Changes happened slowly over many years.
asks: How long did it take to recover?

faq.q: What was the main cause of the Black Death?
faq.a: The main cause was a highly contagious bacterium, which was carried by fleas living on rats. It was a devastating natural event.

facts: The Black Death was a devastating pandemic in the mid-fourteenth century.
It was believed to be carried by fleas living on rats.
The massive loss of life drastically reduced the labor supply.
This scarcity of workers gave surviving laborers more economic bargaining power.

quiz.say: The plague spread most effectively along which type of routes?
quiz.why: Trade routes brought people and goods from far away places together.

wrong.0: While ships moved, the main spread was inland through settlements.
wrong.1: Deserts are too dry and lack the necessary population density.
wrong.3: Mountains were often isolated and did not have the same level of contact.

quiz.say: What was a key consequence for the surviving workers?

options.show: They had to work longer hours for less pay
options.say: They had to work longer hours for less pay

options.show: They left farming for city life
options.say: They left farming for city life

quiz.why: Fewer workers meant their labor was more valuable to landowners.

wrong.1: The opposite happened; they gained more freedom and rights.
wrong.2: Their scarcity allowed them to demand better wages.
wrong.3: While some moved, the core issue was wage negotiation, not just location change.

quiz.say: If labor was scarce, what would happen to the cost of farming?

options.show: The cost would stay exactly the same
options.say: The cost would stay exactly the same

quiz.why: If labor is hard to find, people must pay more money for it.

wrong.1: Falling costs only happen when there is an oversupply of workers.
wrong.2: The massive population drop meant the economy could not remain stable.
wrong.3: Land remained valuable, but the cost of working it changed.
